'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Donbas (2014–2022)|War in Donbass]]
**Two [[Ukrainian Ground Forces|Ukrainian soldiers]] are killed in [[front line]] clashes with [[Russian Separatist forces in Donbas|separatist forces]] in the [[Donbass]], thereby bringing the total number of troops [[killed in action]] this year to 29. Both died due to small arms fire. [https://www.thedefensepost.com/2021/04/12/two-ukrainian-soldiers-killed-east/ (''The Defense Post'')]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Death and funeral of Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh]]
**The [[BBC]] receives a record 110,994 complaints over their coverage of [[Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh|Prince Philip]]'s death, mostly due to the extent of the coverage. [https://www.theguardian.com/media/2021/apr/12/bbcs-prince-philip-coverage-breaks-uk-tv-complaints-record (''The Guardian'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*2021 Peru bus crash
**At least 20 people died in a bus crash in the [[Ancash Region]] in Peru. [https://www.aninews.in/news/world/others/at-least-20-dead-in-bus-accident-in-peru20210413071148/ (ANI)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in the Republic of Ireland]]
*****The [[National Immunisation Advisory Committee]] recommends that the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] should only be given to people over 60 years old following concerns about [[Post-vaccination embolic and thrombotic events|rare blood clot]]s. [https://www.thejournal.ie/astrazeneca-vaccine-ireland-restrictions-niac-recommendation-5407228-Apr2021/ (Thejournal.ie)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 lockdowns|Lockdown]] restrictions are relaxed in [[England]], [[Northern Ireland]], [[Scotland]], and [[Wales]] as the number of cases continues to reduce, with non-essential shops, pubs, gyms, restaurants, hairdressers, community centres, libraries, and theme parks permitted to reopen. Domestic holidays are also permitted again in England with members of the same household. A "stay at home" order is ended in Northern Ireland, and secondary school pupils from years 8–11 return to school. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-56710858 (BBC News)]
****[[Apple Inc|Apple]] and [[Google]] reject an update by the [[National Health Service]] to their [[contact tracing]] [[Application software|app]] because it breaches their privacy rules. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/global-health/science-and-disease/coronavirus-news-lockdown-rules-12-april-easing-covid-vaccine/ (''The Daily Telegraph'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Czech Republic]]
****Schools, libraries, zoos, and some stores in the [[Czech Republic]] reopen after months of closure as the six-month [[state of emergency]] expires and restrictions of movement are lifted. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-czech/czech-schools-shops-reopen-after-long-covid-19-shutdown-idUSKBN2BZ0PB (Reuters)] 
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Greece]]
****High schools in [[Greece]] reopen after five months of closure, with precautions such as wearing masks and [[COVID-19 testing]] for all teachers and students twice per week. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210412-greek-high-schools-reopen-after-five-months-of-closure (France 24)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in India]]
*****[[India]] approves [[Russia]]'s [[Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine|Sputnik V]] [[vaccine]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-india-vaccine-idINKBN2BZ0ZQ (Reuters)]
****[[India]] reports a record for the seventh consecutive day of 168,912 new confirmed cases of COVID-19, thereby bringing the nationwide total of cases to 13.52 million and surpassing Brazil to become the country with the second-highest total of infections. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/india-reports-highest-single-day-rise-of-168-912-new-covid-19-cases-904-deaths-101618198017450.html (''Hindustan Times'')] [https://thehill.com/policy/international/india/547728-india-surpasses-brazil-as-second-most-infected-country (The Hill)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh]]
****[[Bangladesh]] issues new lockdown rules that order the closure of all [[government of Bangladesh|government]], semi-government, autonomous, and private offices for one week beginning April 14, as well as suspension of all [[public transport]]. However, the [[Government of Bangladesh|government]] will allow [[factory|factories]] to remain open. [https://bdnews24.com/bangladesh/2021/04/12/bangladesh-to-shut-all-offices-public-transports-in-new-lockdown-rules (Bdnews24.com)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong]]
****[[Hong Kong]] announces that [[restaurant]]s will be permitted to remain open until midnight and seat more customers, provided that all staff are vaccinated against [[COVID-19]] and all patrons use a government tracking app. [https://www.thestandard.com.hk/breaking-news/section/4/169417/Restaurants-to-open-till-midnight,-only-if-staff-get-vaccinated:-Carrie-Lam (''The Hong Kong Standard'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 985 new confirmed cases of COVID-19, thereby bringing the nationwide total of cases to 33,610. [https://apnews.com/article/lifestyle-pandemics-coronavirus-pandemic-asia-pacific-thailand-98f51655704122467692d4ddd9b9c161 (AP)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario]]
*****[[Premier of Ontario|Ontario Premier]] [[Doug Ford]] announces that all schools across the [[Ontario|province]] will remain closed after April break and students will be forced to shift into online learning amid the rising number of COVID-19 cases and hospitalizations. [https://www.cp24.com/news/all-ontario-schools-will-be-switched-to-remote-only-instruction-following-april-break-1.5384073 (CP24)] 
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]], [[COVID-19 drug development]]
****The [[Federal government of the United States|U.S. government]] terminates a deal with [[Eli Lilly and Company]] for 350,856 remaining doses of the single antibody [[bamlanivimab]] that were scheduled to be delivered by the end of March. The deal will instead be focused on a supply of combined antibodies with [[etesevimab]]. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-04-12/u-s-cancels-deal-for-lilly-s-single-antibody-to-focus-on-combo (Bloomberg)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ghana]]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in Ghana]]
****The [[Ghana Health Service]] says that over 700,000 people in [[Ghana|the country]] has received their first dose of the [[AstraZeneca]] [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://www.ghanaweb.com/GhanaHomePage/NewsArchive/Over-700k-vaccines-dispensed-in-Ghana-1230100 (Ghanaweb)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Solomon Islands]]
***[[Solomon Islands]] receives 50,000 doses of the [[Sinopharm]] [[BBIBP-CorV]] [[vaccine]] from [[China]]. [https://m.solomontimes.com/news/chinas-sinopharm-vaccine-arrives/10755 (''Solomon Times'')]
*[[China]] reports new cases of highly pathogenic [[H5N6]] [[avian influenza|avian flu]] in wild birds in [[Liaoning]], which is the country's first report of the disease since February 2020. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-birdflu-china/china-reports-h5n6-avian-flu-in-wild-birds-in-liaoning-idUSL1N2M51DC (Reuters)]
*[[France|French]] lawmakers vote to ban airlines from offering [[domestic flight]]s if the same journey could be made by [[train]] in less than two and a half hours. [https://www.theguardian.com/business/2021/apr/12/france-ban-some-domestic-flights-train-available-macron-climate-convention-mps (''The Guardian'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Philippines–United States relations]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the military]]
**[[Armed Forces of the Philippines|Philippine]] and [[United States Armed Forces|U.S. troops]] resume their annual [[Balikatan]] [[military exercise]]s following last year's cancellation of the event due to the pandemic. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-philippines-usa-southchinasea/philippines-u-s-to-begin-2-week-joint-military-drill-on-monday-idUSKBN2BY07A (Reuters)]
*[[War in Donbas (2014–2022)|War in Donbass]], [[Ukraine–NATO relations]]
**[[Ukraine]] triggers Article 15 of the Charter on a Special Partnership, initiating an emergency meeting with [[NATO]] to discuss the Russian escalation in [[Donbass]] and the build-up of Russian forces on its [[Russia–Ukraine border|border]]. The article was last triggered in 2018 during the [[Kerch Strait incident]]. [https://ukranews.com/en/news/768973-ukraine-initiates-april-13-emergency-meeting-of-nato-commission-to-discuss-russia-s-escalation-of (Ukranews)]
*[[Cross-Strait relations]]
**[[Taiwan]] reports the largest incursion into its [[air defence identification zone]] to date by [[People's Liberation Army Air Force]] warplanes. Twenty-five aircraft entered its airspace, including nuclear-capable [[Xian H-6|H-6K]] bombers and anti-submarine aircraft. The Chinese fleet flew in an area close to the [[Territorial disputes in the South China Sea|disputed]] [[Pratas Island]], according to Taiwan's Defence Ministry. [https://www.reuters.com/article/taiwan-china-defense/update-1-taiwan-reports-largest-incursion-yet-by-chinese-air-force-idUSL1N2M516J (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2020–21 United States racial unrest]], [[Daunte Wright protests]]
**Tensions between protesters and police intensified for the second night after the [[killing of Daunte Wright]], a 20-year-old man who was shot by police at a traffic stop. [[Minnesota]] Governor [[Tim Walz]] imposes a curfew, and police begin firing gas canisters and flash-bang grenades. Some protesters, wearing gas masks, pick up smoke canisters and throw them back at police. About 40 arrests are made, ranging from curfew violation to rioting. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2021/04/12/daunte-wright-shooting-protests-brooklyn-center-police/7197379002/ (''USA Today'')]
*A gunman on a motorcycle opens fire in front of a [[COVID-19 vaccination]] centre at a [[hospital]] in the [[16th arrondissement of Paris|16th arrondissement]] of [[Paris]], [[France]], killing a man and wounding a female [[security guard]] before riding away. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-france-shooting/one-person-shot-dead-in-front-of-paris-hospital-police-source-idUSKBN2BZ1FP (Reuters)]
*A serving officer with [[London]]'s [[Metropolitan Police]] is sentenced to over two years in prison for an unprovoked attack on a black member of the public that left his victim with a broken leg, in what the judge described as "a clear case of [[racial profiling]]." [https://edition.cnn.com/2021/04/13/uk/met-police-officer-jailed-knee-scli-intl-gbr/index.html (CNN)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Peruvian general election]]
**Far-left candidate [[Pedro Castillo]] is expected to win the first round of the [[president of Peru|presidential]] election. His opponent in the [[runoff election]] in June is still to be determined, amidst a political and [[economy of Peru|economic]] crisis. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-peru-election/peru-presidential-vote-heads-for-run-off-far-left-candidate-leads-idUSKBN2BW27K?il=0 (Reuters)]
